gen-megrim-gf-matemasie: Megrim draws angular, futuristic letters with every stroke ending at one measured thickness, and its c gapes like a bent paperclip. Matemasie follows in sans-serif form, with broad gaps between glyphs and a closed, tidy look.
gen-megrim-gf-menbere: Sharp and sci-fi, with strokes that all stop at the same measured thickness. Megrim handles the dramatic angles, and Menbere stacks its tall lowercase like rolled cord for the quiet work underneath.
gen-megrim-gf-mukta: Angular and futuristic, with curves as thick as a rope's body and an x-height line reaching skyward. Megrim earns its place big and brief.
gen-megrim-gf-rambla: A monoweight skeleton gives Megrim its angular, futuristic edge, with a c as open as a bent paperclip. Rambla comes next with small letters standing nearly as tall as capitals, so shrinking the heading would blur that gap.
gen-megrim-gf-tiny5: Megrim has no calligraphic modulation at all, just angular, futuristic strokes ending at one measured thickness. Tiny5 reads friendly and clean, though its ascenders look short.
gen-megrim-gf-ubuntu: Monoline from stem to serif, Megrim looks angular and futuristic, with a c open like a bent paperclip. Ubuntu follows with a lofty lowercase band, and shrinking the heading would erase that difference.
gen-megrim-gf-yantramanav: Futuristic through and through, Megrim skims along on strokes that never change weight. Yantramanav answers in modern, clean sans-serif, with tall lowercase nearly reaching its capitals and letters huddled close.
gen-megrim-sora: Megrim's angular strokes all end at one measured thickness, and its c opens like a bent paperclip. Sora brings precise, geometric curves with no pressure swell, keeping its c and s widely parted.
gen-mystery-quest-fs-spline-sans: Mystery Quest brings a bookish, nostalgic look, with open jaws on every curved stroke. Spline Sans follows with wide gaps between curve ends and stems, drawn like bent tubing of one gauge, and the heading earns its keep big and short.
gen-mystery-quest-fs-synonym: Open jaws on every curve give Mystery Quest its bookish, nostalgic mood. Mystery Quest does its best work in large, compact lines, while Synonym lays down a constant stripe of ink with generous openings in every curve.
